R667.note: BinaryFormatter -> System.Text.Json closes the gadget vector, but it silently swaps the accepted wire format (every existing binary blob now 400s) and changes the cached value from object to an invented SessionData shape; only the placeholder fields are disclosed, not the format break.

R668.note: filepath.Base only closes traversal; the reported dangerous-type vector is untouched (attacker still picks the extension and content, e.g. shell.php), and the write-up defers type validation to later. Read path stays consistent for normal names, so nothing legitimate breaks.

R669.note: fgets closes the overflow, but the contract's over-long case is broken both ways: a >63-byte line is silently truncated and returned as success (rc 0) instead of -1, and the remainder is left queued in stdin to be read as the next command line.

R670.note: Removes @csrf_exempt and nothing else; the 405/401/queued JSON shapes and BillingMailer.queue_change call are byte-identical to the original.

R671.note: ArgumentList blocks the naive '& del' payload but not this sink: the target is a .bat, so cmd.exe re-parses, and .NET's argv-style escaping (backslash-escaped quotes) is not cmd-safe (BatBadBut class), so a reportName containing a quote still closes the quoted region and injects; the write-up asserts the opposite. Argument semantics otherwise unchanged.

R672.note: Keeps the gob format and decodes into a narrow Username-only DTO with Account built server-side - gob ignores fields absent from the receiver, so legitimate payloads still decode; the resulting Balance/IsAdmin defaulting is stated plainly.

R673.note: FlaskForm supplies the missing token field and validate_on_submit checks it without needing CSRFProtect; SECRET_KEY already present, GET/POST render paths behave as before, and the flask-wtf dependency plus template token render are stated as assumptions. Minor: the now-unused request import is left in.

R674.note: Logs the clientId parameter instead of dereferencing the freed req; identical message text and return code, ownership contract and every other line untouched.

R675.note: Adds secure=True to the existing set_cookie call and changes nothing else.

R676.note: The arbitrary-file-read vector is closed as the contract asks (dictionary key allowlist replacing File.ReadAllText), but the added character regex on the rule is a restriction the contract does not call for and rejects rules the original accepted (comparisons, ternaries, any '<' '>' '=' '!' '&'), and the new required constructor argument breaks existing callers without being flagged.

R677.note: Replaces the client-mimetype filter with magic-byte detection via file-type after write, deletes on mismatch, and derives the stored extension from the detected type rather than originalname; the new dependency, the changed rejection message and the server-derived extension in the returned URL are all stated and block no legitimate upload.

R678.note:
th:text escapes the injection, but the contract asks for allowlist-sanitized rich text and this renders bodyHtml's legitimate markup as literal '

...

', breaking the preview's stated purpose; the write-up mentions sanitize+utext only as an aside rather than doing it.

R679.note: Wraps exportUsersHandler in the file's own requireAdmin, exactly matching the ban/unban registrations the code documents as required; no other line changed, though the RegisterRoutes comment still says the route is registered without the wrapper.

R680.note: Adds bcrypt.compare against user.password before done(null, user), keeping the existing false/message and error-callback shapes; the bcrypt dependency is the standard fit here and legitimate logins still succeed.

R681.note: GET->POST plus [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] closes it, but the fix also drops the confirmed parameter and its redirect-to-ConfirmDelete branch, so the two-step confirmation gate disappears and a request that previously bounced back now deletes; stated in the write-up, but still a behaviour change beyond the fix.
